methods.title: File-Based Project Memory
methods.description: The baseline is the actual ProjectMemoryRail. Facts are written to an isolated JIUWENSWARM.md file. Its prompt includes file metadata and is truncated to the full-section character budget. Both arms receive the same facts, questions, model, system prompt and no tools. This is not a retrieval-augmented embedding baseline.

methods.title: Hybrid Selection from Working Memory
methods.description: EnhancedMemoryRail writes completed user-assistant exchanges to process-local L1 memory. The experiment uses lexical Jaccard similarity combined with temporal decay, access frequency and importance, rather than learned embeddings. Selected memories are assembled under the same full-section character budget. The architecture has L2/L3 classes, but this Rail does not route writes there, persist them across process restarts or synchronize a team. MemGPT is conceptual context, not an implemented or tested baseline.

methods.title: Isolation and Cost Accounting
methods.description: Each public-data question has its own fact episode and fresh agents. Baseline writes facts to disk; enhanced performs model-backed memory-writing conversations. The formal question uses a new conversation ID. The runner verifies isolated query history and actual memory injection, alternates arm order across questions, and records both query usage and memory-write usage. Latency including writes is amortized over paired observations. Correctness is accepted-answer string matching; evidence recall requires the complete target fact to survive prompt truncation.

source_notes.memgpt: Verified arXiv abstract: virtual context management inspired by operating-system hierarchies moves information across memory tiers; demonstrations include document analysis and multi-session chat. Our fixed L1 Rail does not implement its autonomous virtual-memory controller.
source_notes.longmemeval: Verified arXiv abstract: LongMemEval evaluates extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, updates and abstention; it separates indexing, retrieval and reading. The submitted small single-session-user adaptation covers only a narrow slice, not the official full benchmark.
source_notes.generative_agents: Verified arXiv abstract: natural-language experience records are synthesized into reflections and dynamically retrieved for planning behavior in an interactive simulation. This study neither implements reflection/planning nor tests social behavior; distinguish record retrieval from that broader architecture.
source_notes.lost_middle: Verified arXiv abstract: relevant information position affects multi-document QA and key-value retrieval in long contexts, with middle positions often harder. This motivates attention to information access but does not establish that our observed prefix truncation is caused by the same phenomenon.
source_notes.memorybank: Verified arXiv abstract: MemoryBank supports retrieval and updates for sustained personalized interaction, with forgetting and reinforcement influenced by elapsed time and importance. Our temporal ranking is a simple heuristic, not a replication of MemoryBank or its companionship evaluation.
source_notes.amem: Verified arXiv abstract: A-MEM creates structured notes and dynamically links and evolves memories, inspired by Zettelkasten organization. Our fixed lexical ranking lacks autonomous linking and evolution; no empirical comparison to A-MEM was run.

title: Evaluating Memory Retrieval: Evidence Quality and Lifecycle Cost
research_question: Under matched token budgets and controlled memory representations, how do selection and construction affect answer quality and lifecycle cost across repeated queries?

research_questions.title: Quality under Matched Budgets
research_questions.question: How does answer and evidence quality compare against stronger baselines with identical representations, formatting and token accounting?

research_questions.title: Attributing Component Effects
research_questions.question: Which differences remain when selection, representation and construction are varied separately?

research_questions.title: Lifecycle Cost under Memory Reuse
research_questions.question: How does measured write-plus-query cost change when a constructed memory serves multiple distinct queries?

writing_notes: This is a revision plan, not a completed revised paper. Frame the contribution as an auditable empirical systems evaluation, without claiming a novel retrieval algorithm.

Existing public_small and public_large files remain pilot observations with character budgets, different construction and formatting, and a single run per budget. They cannot answer the new controlled research questions.
All new experiments are planned. Proposed token budgets, repetition counts and reuse counts are design choices, not observed measurements or approved experimental scale.

Confirm tokenizer and model versions, dataset revision and sample size, scorer version and statistical implementation with the experiment owner before running. Missing fields are deliberately omitted and reported.
The benchmark-protocol replication is a task to implement and verify, not a claim of current official LongMemEval compliance.
Do not claim significance, a break-even point, better generalization, or resolution of reviewer concerns before new evidence is reviewed.
Keep the existing implemented-method descriptions separate from candidate baselines and changes proposed in experiment protocols.
Use the general content renderer until new multi-arm and repeated-query evidence parsers and assets are implemented. The existing research assets describe only the audited L1 pilot.

reuse.construction_cost_policy: Measure one construction per memory instance and count it once: total = write + sum(query); per-query = total / query count. Freeze query-side mutation. Report failures and all usage; distinguish observed totals from extrapolation.

review_concerns.title: Weak Baseline and Budget Confounding
review_concerns.description: Match token accounting, representation and formatting; compare against stronger selectors before attributing gains to retrieval.

review_concerns.title: Construction, Representation and Selection Confounds
review_concerns.description: Change one component per ablation and preserve control traces; budget sensitivity alone is not a component ablation.

review_concerns.title: Unmeasured Memory Reuse
review_concerns.description: Measure multiple distinct queries against one built memory and count construction once.

review_concerns.title: Small Single-Run Sample and Scoring Limitations
review_concerns.description: Predeclare a broader evaluation, repeat runs, review scoring, account for dependence and verify benchmark protocol alignment.

review_concerns.title: Limited Algorithmic Novelty
review_concerns.description: Scope the contribution as a controlled and reproducible lifecycle-cost study. Better prose does not create a new retrieval algorithm, and these experiments do not guarantee acceptance.
